author: Brian Platt, Thomas Seal
description: Prime Minister Mark Carney said his support of US action to prevent Iran getting nuclear weapons came “with regret” because the current conflict is a new example of the failure of the international order.
title: Carney Urges US, Israel to Respect Rules of Engagement in Iran

description: President Trump said Tuesday that an attack on Iran’s leadership was “pretty substantial,” but declined to provide further details. Meanwhile, during a White House meeting with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, Trump instructed Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to “cut off all trade with Spain.” Trump also criticized the UK for blocking his request to use the military base on Diego Garcia for strikes on Iran. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Clerical Body Targeted; Trump Spars With UK, Spain

author: Sarah Holder, Rachael Lewis-Krisky
description: On today’s Big Take: As the war with Iran widens in the Middle East, tensions are rising on Capitol Hill.
title: The White House’s Shifting Explanations for the Iran War

description: President Donald Trump is worried about who could run Iran next. “I guess the worst case would be, we do this, and then somebody takes over, who’s as bad as the previous person, right? That could happen,” Trump told reporters Tuesday in the Oval Office. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Worried an Even Worse Leader Could Take Over Iran

author: Amara Omeokwe
description: War and the economy may make some Fed policymakers more cautious.
title: Trump’s Fed Chair Pick Faces Obstacles to Delivering on Rate Cuts

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec discuss a risk-off move gripping markets to start Tuesday as investors digest Iran war headwinds. Brookfield Asset Management CEO Connor Teskey weighs in from Bloomberg Invest, and also discusses the state of private credit. Then, Bloomberg's Eric Weiner recaps today's price action as stocks and bonds sink and oil rallies. Plus, NYSE President Lynn Martin weighs in on the IPO backdrop as candidates look to get deals done amid geopolitical uncertainty. Next, MongoDB CEO CJ Desai on the company's recent earnings and investor worries as the stock sinks as far as 20% Tuesday. Finally, Ariel Investments Founder & CEO John Rogers on value investing and the US consumer. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Businessweek Live at Bloomberg Invest | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/03/2026

author: Arne Delfs
description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told President Donald Trump that he wants the European Union’s trade agreement with the US to be implemented quickly but the bloc can’t accept a deal with worse conditions.
title: Merz Says EU Won’t Accept US Trade Deal on Worse Tariff Terms

author: Sherif Tarek
description: A drone attack caused a “limited” fire near the US consulate in Dubai, the latest American diplomatic facility in the Persian Gulf to be targeted during the war with Iran.
title: Drone Attack Causes ‘Limited’ Fire Near US Consulate in Dubai

description: President Donald Trump says the US will escort oil tankers and other vessels through the Strait of Hormuz if needed. Energy prices stabilized. Rebecca Babin of CIBC Private Wealth says "crude needed this headline." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Promises to Secure Oil Tankers Through Hormuz Amid Iran War

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the continued conflict in the Middle East. On today's show, Stimson Center Senior Fellow Kelly Grieco, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Democractic Congressman Bill Foster of Illinois and Cook Political Report Editor Jessica Taylor. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Questions Future Iran Leaders | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/03/2026

author: Layan Odeh
description: The US war in Iran hasn’t changed Brookfield Asset Management’s plans to build data centers with the Qatar Investment Authority or curbed its appetite for investing in the Middle East, Chief Executive Officer Connor Teskey said.
title: Brookfield Says Iran War Won’t Affect Its $20 Billion Qatar Deal

author: Erik Wasson
description: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to an interview with the House Oversight Committee over his ties to disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein, the panel’s chairman said.
title: Lutnick Plans to Testify About Epstein Ties to House Panel

description: Ariel Investments co-CEO John Rogers says he does see the risk of a small recession on the horizon in the US because so many Americans are struggling. He speaks to Bloomberg Television at Bloomberg Invest.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Ariel's Rogers Sees Small Risk of US Recession

description: NYSE Group Inc. President Lynn Martin says geopolitical risks and global conflicts like the current one in Iran are unlikely to stop companies from going public. She spoke to Bloomberg Television on Tuesday at the Bloomberg Invest conference in New York. “And if you’re a good company, you can always go public." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Good Companies Can Always Go Public, NYSE's Martin Says

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Ben Bartenstein, Ari Natter
description: President Donald Trump said the US will provide insurance guarantees and naval escorts to ensure safe passage for oil tankers and other vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, aiming to head off a potential energy crisis caused by the war with Iran.
title: Trump Says US Will Escort, Insure Oil Tankers Amid Iran War

author: Katherine Doherty
description: Global conflicts, including the strikes on Iran over the past week, are unlikely to put a complete stop to companies tapping the US public markets, according to NYSE Group Inc. President Lynn Martin said.
title: Geopolitics Unlikely to Put a Stop to IPOs, NYSE’s Martin Says

description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Matt Miller and Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Bloomberg Open Interest is on the road at Bloomberg Invest Conference, where the power players shaping the future of money take center stage. From Apollo’s Marc Rowan and Ares CEO Mike Arougheti to Soros Fund’s Dawn Fitzpatrick and Goldman’s Vivek Bantwal — we’re zeroing in on the explosive rise of private markets and private credit as geopolitics drives volatility. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Bloomberg Invest: Finance Power Players | Open Interest 3/3/2026

author: Natalia Drozdiak
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio sparked fresh criticism over the Trump administration’s shifting rationale for the Iran war after he suggested that Israel’s determination to strike the country had forced the US to act.
title: Rubio Spurs Backlash With Latest Rationale for Attacks on Iran

author: Samy Adghirni, Benoit Berthelot, Kavita Mokha
description: French President Emmanuel Macron said he’ll send an aircraft carrier to the Mediterranean to help secure maritime routes and ensure Europe’s economic interests in the region.
title: Macron to Deploy Aircraft Carrier to Shield Mideast Shipping

author: Rodrigo Orihuela
description: Spain should work with the European Union when making setting its position on large international matters, the country’s largest business group said.
title: Spain Must Work With EU on Global Affairs, Business Group Says

description: President Donald Trump expressed concern that the strikes against Iran could lead to a new leadership that’s equally troubling to Washington as the regime the US and Israel are fighting to topple.
title: Trump Worries Iran’s Leaders May Be Just ‘as Bad’ After War

description: Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem faced bipartisan criticism Tuesday over federal immigration operations that left two American citizens dead in Minneapolis, as a Republican senator threatened to block Trump administration nominees and Democrats pressed her to acknowledge making mistakes.
title: Noem Faces Bipartisan Rebuke Over Deadly Immigration Operation

author: Tyler Kendall
description: US President Donald Trump directed Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to “cut off all trade with Spain” after the country denied access to its military bases for his bombing campaign against Iran.

author: Stephanie Hughes
description: Canadian equities stumbled on Tuesday, by the most since April’s tariff-fueled market rout, as an escalating war in the Middle East unnerved investors who exited even traditional safe havens like gold and energy stocks.
title: Canadian Stocks Sink Most Since Tariff Chaos as Miners Sell Off

author: Dan Williams
description: Israeli forces seized new positions in south Lebanon for the first time since a 2024 truce, as their attacks on Hezbollah intensified in parallel with the war against Iran.

description: President Donald Trump says an attack on Iran's leadership Tuesday was "pretty substantial." He says Iran has no air protection or detection facilities left. He speaks in the Oval Office.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says Iran Is In for 'a Lot of Hurt'

author: Catarina Saraiva, Michael McKee
description: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari, who had penciled in one interest-rate cut this year, said the attacks on Iran make him less certain about that.
title: Fed’s Kashkari Says War Creates Uncertainty for Rate Path

author: Jeff Mason, Tyler Kendall
description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he intended to discuss with President Donald Trump the next steps in the war on Iran amid questions about the US administration’s endgame after it launched strikes on the Islamic Republic.

description: New York City’s congestion pricing program can continue after a federal judge ruled that the Trump administration’s attempts to terminate it were unlawful — a financial win for the nation’s largest mass transit provider.

description: The response to bolster the Mediterranean island comes as resources are already stretched by the conflict in Ukraine.

description: President Donald Trump is unlikely to be constrained by the Republican-led Congress on the war in Iran anytime soon.

description: New York Governor Kathy Hochul and Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced the first communities that will offer free child care for toddlers starting this fall.

description: Canada is moving closer to deploying around C$3.5 billion ($2.6 billion) in investments and programs to accelerate development of critical minerals deposits.

description: Russia is dismayed by US and Israeli attacks on Iran but mostly powerless to aid its ally, and sees potential benefits for President Vladimir Putin’s war on Ukraine, according to five people familiar with the matter.

description: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban is leveraging the US-Israeli war on Iran in his latest bid to close a wide opposition poll lead with a general election weeks away.

Saudi Arabia is being dragged deeper into the Middle East crisis after Iranian attacks on the US embassy in Riyadh and on the kingdom's largest oil refinery. 

Paul Wallace explains.

description: Representative Ro Khanna is facing backlash from billionaires for supporting a California wealth tax. Now a tech entrepreneur wants to turn that anger into a June primary challenge for Khanna’s Silicon Valley seat.

description: The biggest contest of the 2026 midterm election cycle so far is underway, with voters in Texas making their choices in a statewide primary Tuesday that could determine whether Democrats have a shot at narrowing the gap with Republicans in the US Senate come November.

description:
Two drones struck near the US Embassy in Riyadh, pulling Saudi Arabia into a widening conflict among Iran, the US and Israel.

(Removes footage retracted by the Associated Press.) (Source: Bloomberg)

description: Kevin Warsh is still months away from taking the helm at the Federal Reserve, but his ability to deliver the interest-rate cuts President Donald Trump expects is facing hurdles as the US economy, and his future colleagues, tilt in the opposite direction.
title: Even Before He Reaches the Fed, Warsh’s Path to Rate Cuts Is Getting Tougher

description: Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves will use her economic statement today to lament that the world is awash with uncertainty. This time, responding to the latest economic forecasts from the Office for Budget Responsibility, the UK’s fiscal watchdog, the chancellor will flag the importance of “stability in the public finances, investment in infrastructure and reform to our economy.” Bloomberg's Lizzy Burden reports from Westminster. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: UK's Reeves Set to Respond to Latest Economic Forecasts

description: Global energy markets have been upended by the Iran conflict which erupted on Saturday and then spread across the oil-rich Middle East. Oil’s metrics point to intense near-term tightness, as Bloomberg's Rong Wei Neo explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

description: Inflation is re-emerging as the crucial worry in the $30 trillion Treasuries market amid concerns of a potential protracted conflict in the Middle East that keeps crude prices elevated. Bloomberg's Mark Cranfield breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

description: The US sent conflicting messages about how long a war with Iran might last as Israel launched new airstrikes on Tuesday, with the widening conflict reverberating across the Middle East and upending energy markets.

description: The Bank of Russia has filed a claim with the European Union over the bloc’s decision to seize its assets, escalating a dispute over sanctions imposed after Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine.
title: Russia’s Central Bank Sues EU in Luxembourg Over Frozen Assets

description: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said a special committee investigating anti-graft chief Azam Baki’s shareholdings will submit its report soon, and it’s therefore too early to decide on the need for a Royal Commission of Inquiry into allegations the agency colluded with businessmen to oust company founders.
title: Malaysia’s Anwar Says Panel Probing Graft Chief Will Report Soon

author: Jana Randow
description: The next four weeks will determine whether Europe’s economy is facing a fresh crisis or simply a speed bump in its recovery.

author: Sakura Murakami
description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said she’ll have frank talks on Iran when she meets US President Donald Trump in Washington later this month.
title: Japan’s Takaichi Aims to Have Frank Talks With Trump on Iran

author: Lucille Liu, Jenny Leonard, Eric Martin
description: US and Chinese trade negotiators are slated to meet in mid-March, according to people familiar with the matter, signaling a planned summit between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping is pushing ahead despite American strikes against Iran.
title: US, China Trade Chiefs to Meet Mid-March Before Trump-Xi Summit

author: Cliff Harvey Venzon, Ditas B Lopez
description: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. sought to allay concerns about the economic impact of the war in the Middle East, as his government finds ways to ensure the safety of millions of Filipino workers in the region.

description: The US sent conflicting messages about how long a war with Iran might last as Israel launched new airstrikes on Monday, with the widening conflict reverberating across the Middle East and upending energy markets. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday rejected the idea of an “endless” war with Iran. But President Donald Trump later insisted there was no fixed timeline. Both refused to rule out putting American boots on the ground. Ed Price, a senior non-resident fellow at New York University, discusses the longstanding pretext for the armed conflict and how it might unfold with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec on Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Vows ‘Whatever It Takes’ on Iran as Conflict Widens

author: Ainsley Thomson
description: New Zealand’s Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said he misspoke when he stated that his center-right government supported “any actions” to prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons, further muddying his message on the Middle East conflict.

description: Aluminum edged up after US President Donald Trump suggested the military campaign against Iran could last weeks, raising the risk of deeper disruptions to exports of the metal from the Middle East.
title: Aluminum Holds Gain as Iran Conflict Roils Global Supplies

description: Congressional Democrats are vowing to contest the Trump administration’s unprecedented actions against the artificial intelligence giant Anthropic PBC, which include a prohibition on all use in the federal government and by Pentagon contractors.

description: OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman said that the company’s rush to forge a deal with the Defense Department — following a clash between the Pentagon and rival Anthropic PBC — looked “opportunistic and sloppy.”

description: Two drones struck near the US Embassy in Riyadh, pulling Saudi Arabia into a widening conflict among Iran, the US and Israel, and prompting President Donald Trump to vow retaliation.

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Gabe Amo (D-RI) shares his reaction to the US-Israel strikes on Iran and criticizes the Trump Administration with what he calls shifting justifications for their actions. Michael Allen, Beacon Global Strategies Managing Director, questions the outlook for a diplomatic solution in regards to the strikes and warns Tehran’s strongest leverage may be disrupting energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: War Powers Debate Escalates After US Strike on Iran | Balance of Show: Late Edition 03/02/2026

title: Iran Retaliates Following US-Israel Strikes

author: Joe Mayes
description: Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves will use her economic statement on Tuesday to lament that the world is awash with uncertainty. And she’ll try not to contribute any more of it — by saying as little as possible.
